author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 전국에 흔히 찾아와 겨울을 나는 겨울철새로, 침엽수림과 낙엽활엽수림에서 지낸다. 겨울에는 10~30마리, 때로는 100마리에 이르는 무리를 지어 주로 나무 위에서 생활한다. 식물성 먹이를 주로 먹고 파리목 곤충도 먹는다. 구북구 북부와 신북구 서북부에서 번식하며, 6월경 한배에 알 4~6개, 보통 5개를 낳고 때로 7개를 낳기도 한다.

art.subject: Bohemian Waxwing (Bombycilla garrulus), adult male in winter, as seen in flocks in Korean woodland and parks from November to March: plumage soft pinkish grey-brown, greyer on the rump; forehead and forecrown warm apricot-chestnut; a long soft crest swept back from the crown; a narrow black mask from the bill base through the eye and a neat black chin and throat bib with a sharp lower edge; undertail coverts chestnut; wings blackish with white tips to the primary coverts, a white-and-yellow edge along the tips of the primaries and small red waxy tips on the secondaries; tail grey shading to black with a broad yellow tip; short stout black bill with a little white at the gape; dark eye; black legs.
art.pose: perched in a treetop with a flock, side view
art.scene: Korean winter conifer and deciduous broadleaf woodland with bare branches; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched on a berry-laden twig: pinkish grey-brown body, chestnut forehead, long swept-back crest, black mask and bib, wing with white and yellow tips and red waxy tips, broad yellow tail tip, chestnut undertail, black legs
adult, head detail in side view: apricot-chestnut forehead and forecrown, long soft crest from crown to nape, narrow black mask and black throat, short black bill with white only at the gape
adult female, side view perched: like the male but the black throat patch smaller with a diffuse lower edge, narrower yellow tail band and less yellow on the wingtips
art.build: Plump, starling-shaped songbird, 18-20cm, about the size of a Common Starling but softer-looking, with a short neck, a big swept-back crest and a short square tail. Bill short, stout and slightly hooked, much shorter than the head. Legs short and black. Wings long and pointed; in flight the triangular wings and short tail look starling-like. Sits upright in tight flocks at the top of trees and gorges on berries.
avoid: Do not paint a red tail tip, or a wing without red waxy tips and with a red-tinged bar - those are Japanese Waxwing (Bombycilla japonica).
Do not paint grey undertail coverts; they are chestnut.
Do not shorten or omit the crest; it is long and swept back.
Do not give it a thin warbler-like bill or a long tail.
